correctness.rationale: All quantifiers are explicit for every nonempty word over each finite alphabet of at least two symbols. The interval envelope F/G gives the optimal terminal probability because each letter transition is nondecreasing. Monotonicity of the extremal orbit plus affine sign interpolation forbids reappearance of a letter in a unique winner. Conversely, the explicit rational maps f_{i+1}=f_i+eps(x-c_i) have increasing crossing points, strictly maximal planned letter at every reachable orbit state, valid row-stochastic matrices, and strictly increasing F; competitors remain strictly below. The construction was independently exercised using exact Fraction arithmetic on 103 block profiles and 416353 explicit competitor words.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The universal three-state bound does not imply two-state sufficiency. Binary classifications do not imply existence for words with at least three distinct occurring letters. This theorem is limited to order-preserving two-state PFAs; a stronger unrestricted classification, if found, could subsume it, but no such source was identified.

originality.rationale: In arXiv:2402.13376 Theorem 4.1 addresses only binary input words and Section 4.4 only embeds binary witnesses into larger alphabets. In arXiv:2607.26275 Proposition 4.1 shows universal three-state sufficiency, while Remark 5.3 explicitly leaves the multi-symbol two-state classification open. Neither implies rational order-preserving two-state witnesses for every word with arbitrarily many distinct blocks, nor the exact converse for such witnesses. Mathematical record queries returned no direct covering claim.

value.rationale: The finite-alphabet two-state classification is explicitly open in the recent primary reference. This theorem identifies an exact, natural, maximal-by-classification structural family for order-preserving two-state machines and supplies rational witnesses for all words of arbitrarily many distinct letter blocks. It distinguishes positive-slope from order-reversing mechanisms rather than yielding a routine alphabet relabeling of the binary result.
